accepted.basis: Subject-verb agreement rule: a plural subject takes a plural verb form.
accepted.original: Cell cultures was maintained at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 [12].
accepted.reason: Subject 'cultures' is plural, so the verb must be 'were', not 'was'.
accepted.revised: Cell cultures were maintained at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 [12].

accepted.basis: Methods-section tense convention: completed experimental steps in past tense.
accepted.original: The medium is replaced every 48 h and cells were passaged at 80% confluence.
accepted.reason: Methods describe completed procedures; present 'is' is shifted to past 'was' for tense consistency with the rest of the sentence.
accepted.revised: The medium was replaced every 48 h and cells were passaged at 80% confluence.

accepted.basis: Article usage rule: singular countable nouns take an article when not pluralized or possessive.
accepted.original: The absorbance was measured at wavelength of 450 nm using a microplate reader.
accepted.reason: The singular countable noun 'wavelength' requires the indefinite article 'a' in this context.
accepted.revised: The absorbance was measured at a wavelength of 450 nm using a microplate reader.

accepted.basis: Dangling-modifier rule: an introductory participial phrase must modify the subject that follows it.
accepted.original: Using ImageJ software, the images were analyzed to quantify colony formation.
accepted.reason: The introductory phrase 'Using ImageJ software' dangles: its implied agent cannot be 'the images'. Naming the agent 'we' resolves it.
accepted.revised: Using ImageJ software, we analyzed the images to quantify colony formation.

accepted.basis: Academic register guideline: avoid colloquial quantifiers ('a bunch of') and vague verbs ('worked').
accepted.original: We did a bunch of tests to check whether the treatment worked.
accepted.reason: 'did a bunch of tests' and 'worked' are colloquial; they are replaced with formal academic equivalents.
accepted.revised: We performed a series of assays to determine whether the treatment was effective.

accepted.basis: Hedging guideline: claim strength must match the strength and scope of the evidence.
accepted.original: These results prove that the new protocol is perfect for all cell types.
accepted.reason: 'prove' and 'perfect for all cell types' claim more than the data support; the claim is hedged to match the evidence scope.
accepted.revised: These results suggest that the new protocol is effective for the cell types tested.

accepted.basis: Conciseness rule: replace multi-word connectives with single-word equivalents when meaning is unchanged.
accepted.original: Due to the fact that the signal was weak at this point in time, the exposure time was increased to 30 s.
accepted.reason: 'Due to the fact that' and 'at this point in time' are redundant wordy phrases replaced by concise equivalents without meaning change.
accepted.revised: Because the signal was weak, the exposure time was increased to 30 s.

accepted.basis: Comma rule: use a comma before the conjunctive adverb 'then' joining sequential clauses.
accepted.original: The samples were heated to 95 °C for 10 min then cooled on ice.
accepted.reason: A comma is required before 'then' when it links two sequential actions in one sentence.
accepted.revised: The samples were heated to 95 °C for 10 min, then cooled on ice.

accepted.basis: Semicolon rule: a semicolon may join two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.
accepted.original: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and representative images are shown in Fig. 2.
accepted.reason: A semicolon tightens the link between two closely related independent clauses here.
accepted.revised: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05; representative images are shown in Fig. 2.

edit.original: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, and representative images are shown in Fig. 2.
edit.revised: Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, with representative images in Fig. 2.
